out.reasoning: Central banks commonly hold for several meetings after explicitly ending an easing cycle. Banxico ended its cycle in May, removed its easing bias, and unanimously held at 6.50% in June. BBVA expects an extended hold and regards the rate as neutral. As of July 23, falling headline inflation and core inflation of 3.95% substantially reduce the case for a hike. They could support renewed cuts, particularly given weak growth, but reversing recent guidance would likely require stronger evidence than the modest latest downside inflation surprise. Only two weeks remain until August 6. A sharp deterioration in activity or further disinflation could trigger a cut; a currency or inflation shock could revive tightening pressure. With neither evident in the frozen record, another hold is strongly favored.
